correctness.rationale: Five query rows give eleven F2^5 coordinate profiles; each pair-of-coordinates parity returns their XOR. Shattering all 32 patterns requires zero from a duplicated profile plus all 31 nonzero differences from >=10 distinct profiles. Any ten-difference basis has full affine span and admits a six-point affine frame sent to (0,1,2,4,8,16); hence exactly C(26,4)=14950 normalized ten-sets and C(26,3)=2600 normalized nine-sets exhaust possibilities. Independent complete enumeration yielded exactly 80 covering ten-sets, no covering nine-set, and 80640 independent affine frames within A0; all 80 normalized images occur from A0. Exactly 1008 frame maps stabilize A0, with orbit size 317440 and point orbits sizes 7 and 3. Seven XOR-zero affine planes distinguish duplicate choices by 4 versus 0 incidences. The completeness reduction, not an incomplete brute force, justifies classification.

value.rationale: A natural extremal VC-shattering witness classification, not arbitrary numerical enumeration: it completely determines which minimal five-query supports occur for a sparse parity hypothesis class and the exact symmetry types of repeats. The affine normalization plus stabilizer-orbit structure is reusable for comparison of extremal binary additive designs.
residual_risks: Only dimension five and eleven columns; does not imply an asymptotic classification, but exact first-threshold designs are meaningful.

final_claim: The ten-element additive-difference bases of F2^5 form a single affine orbit of 317440 sets (stabilizer 1008); extremal five-query shattering by 55 two-coordinate parities on 11 positions has precisely two affine classes of repeated profile, with stabilizer orbits of sizes seven and three.
limitations: Classification only under AGL(5,2) and coordinate permutations, not five-query index permutations or arbitrary sparse degrees.
Some prior finite-difference-basis literature may have equivalent orbit counts not indexed by published title.
